title: Fortnite-maker Epic Games confirms 'huge pivot' towards using AI
key_facts: Epic Games, maker of Fortnite, is making a "huge pivot" towards AI in video game development, according to chief executive Tim Sweeney.
Sweeney said on social media that developers are being moved to "retool for maximum AI acceleration".

Bloomberg reported that Epic delayed a collaboration with Disney featuring Star Wars and Marvel characters and that developers were asked to use AI tools to finish it; directors reportedly said "no more hand-written code" and art would be "generated with full AI workflows".
Sweeney did not publicly comment on the Disney collaboration; BBC Newsbeat has approached Epic.
Sweeney said the purpose is not "to do the same stuff with fewer people" but to give developers tools to build "more" and "better stuff", and called it a "modest aim to survive the AI revolution".
The news comes six months after Epic laid off more than 1,000 employees, which Sweeney then attributed to a downturn in Fortnite engagement, not AI.

A game designer who does not work for Epic told the BBC she is not completely against AI but that generated art is "taking away" artists' jobs; in 2025 actors' union Sag-Aftra filed a complaint over AI recreating Darth Vader's voice in Fortnite.
quote_evidence: Fortnite-maker Epic Games is making a "huge pivot" towards using artificial intelligence (AI) in its video game development, according to boss Tim Sweeney.
The US firm's CEO made the announcement on social media, saying developers are being moved to "retool for maximum AI acceleration".
The news comes six months after Epic confirmed it was laying off more than 1,000 employees.
why_it_matters_hint: A major games studio is openly reorienting its development around AI, in an industry where artists and developers fear job losses.
event_date: Reported 13 Oct 2026; date of Sweeney's posts not stated
notes: Sweeney's own posts confirm the pivot; the Disney delay and the "no more hand-written code" directive are Bloomberg's reporting as relayed by the BBC. The date of the posts is not stated, so the entry is marked NEW.
